title: A name, not a booking reference
subtitle: What being known to a cruise line is worth on the day you actually need something.

text: Lines keep records on advisors, much as they do on ships.
sub: How much we sell, how well we brief a client, how rarely we ring in a panic. That standing decides whether a request is looked at or merely logged.

items.head: The upgrade nobody advertises
items.body: Suites move quietly close to sailing. They move towards people the line can reach in an afternoon.

items.head: Position on the waitlist
items.body: Every full sailing has a queue. Where you sit in it is not always first come, first served.

items.head: The exception
items.body: Dining, connecting cabins, a deposit held a little longer. Discretionary - and discretion is a relationship.

items.head: The escalation
items.body: When a decision is needed above the call centre, somebody has to know exactly whom to ask.

right.label: A name
items: A known desk, a direct line

quote: Every fare I quote is one I've negotiated. My clients never pay retail.

text: Trade access is leverage you cannot buy at a checkout.
sub: A Virtuoso practice brings contracted space, credits and access that exist only through the trade. None of it appears anywhere on a booking page.

title: Save this for the next "the price is the price"
body: Or write to me with a sailing you are weighing up, and I'll tell you what is available on it that the booking page will not show you.
